tasks.title: Member auth foundation (verify Bearer JWT)
tasks.description: READ .softhouse/auth-profile-brief.md IN FULL (esp. the SECURITY REQUIREMENTS) + root.yaml memberOAuth2 + app/api/deps.py (existing get_session + bootstrap-token dep). Build the member-auth FOUNDATION: a JWT VERIFIER behind a port (verify an RS256 Bearer JWT against the IdP public key/JWKS) + a DEV/TEST RS signer (test-only keypair to mint tokens for the suite; clearly marked dev-only, never a prod secret). A FastAPI dependency `get_current_member(session)` that: extracts the Bearer token, verifies signature with the configured PUBLIC key, ACCEPTS ONLY alg=RS256 (REJECT alg:none and HS256 — no header-chosen alg/key), enforces exp/nbf and iss/aud where configured, resolves the token `sub` to a Member row (401 missing/invalid token; 401/403 unknown subject), and returns the Member. Add the JWT dep to pyproject (PyJWT[crypto] or equiv — do NOT hand-roll crypto). NO endpoint yet beyond what proves the dep (a tiny protected probe is fine, or leave the endpoint to T2). Tests backend/tests/test_auth.py: valid token -> member; expired -> 401; bad signature -> 401; alg:none -> 401; HS256-signed-with-pubkey-as-secret -> 401 (algorithm confusion); unknown sub -> 401/403. NO money/ledger. GATES from backend/ ALL PASS: check_models, check_migration, openapi/validate.py, pytest; ruff+mypy strict clean on new files. Handoff: the verifier design, the EXACT algorithm+claim checks and which attacks are rejected, the dev-signer approach, gate outputs.

tasks.title: Security review — auth foundation
tasks.description: INDEPENDENT SECURITY review of T1 (JWT verification is attacker-facing — be adversarial). In your worktree `git checkout` the branch, `cd backend`, RUN all 4 gates yourself (paste verdicts). Read .softhouse/auth-profile-brief.md, root.yaml memberOAuth2, the handoff .softhouse/handoff/20260728-auth-profile/T1.md, `git diff main...<branch>`, and the verifier source. ATTACK IT: (1) is the signature ACTUALLY verified (not decode-without-verify)? (2) is the algorithm PINNED to RS256 server-side — does an `alg:none` token pass? does an HS256 token signed with the RS public key as the HMAC secret pass (the classic key-confusion)? does the code EVER read the algorithm from the token header to choose the key? Any yes = REJECT. (3) exp enforced? nbf? iss/aud validated where configured? (4) is `sub` resolved to a DB Member (not trusted as a member fact from the claim)? (5) any token/claim/secret logged? is the dev/test keypair clearly test-only and not a usable prod secret? (6) does the test suite actually exercise alg:none + HS256-confusion + expired + bad-sig + unknown-sub, and would those tests FAIL if the verifier were permissive (non-vacuous)? Confirm ruff+mypy clean on new files. Verdict APPROVED/MICRO-FIX/REJECTED with the specific attack that succeeds if any.
